purpose: SOTA-first reproduction of TimeFilter on the official processed ECL (RP90-RP97)

source.reference: TimeFilter (Hu et al., ICML 2025, arXiv:2501.13041), author code github.com/TROUBADOUR000/TimeFilter

benchmark_contract.target: all 321 client series (features M: every channel is input and target; 'OT' is client 320 renamed by the distributor)
benchmark_contract.target_construction: hourly consumption values as distributed (Autoformer/TimesNet processed ECL); nothing aggregated here
benchmark_contract.split_rule: chronological: train rows [0, 18412), vali rows [18412-L, 18412+2632), test rows [26304-5260-L, 26304); Dataset_Custom borders of the author loader
benchmark_contract.missing_policy: none needed: the distributed file has no missing values (receipted)
benchmark_contract.scaler_fit_population: StandardScaler fit on the train rows [0, train) of every channel; applied to all rows
benchmark_contract.metric_formula: MSE = mean (yhat - y)^2 and MAE = mean |yhat - y| over every test window x horizon step x channel, normalized space
benchmark_contract.metric_aggregation: one mean over all elements of the test set per horizon; the paper also averages the four horizons
benchmark_contract.naive_baseline: persistence of the last observed value of the window at every step and channel, same windows
benchmark_contract.permitted_inputs: the L-step window of all 321 channels (plus the loader's calendar marks, unused by the model)
benchmark_contract.tuning_budget: none: the author script's settings, frozen
benchmark_contract.checkpoint_selection: lowest validation MSE epoch, EarlyStopping patience 3, restored

comparability.why: every identity field matches; the paper's metric is reported first

reference_evidence.why: no reference run root was given

lock.paper: Hu, Y. et al. TimeFilter: Patch-Specific Spatial-Temporal Graph Filtration for Time Series Forecasting. ICML 2025 (PMLR v267); arXiv:2501.13041. Author code github.com/TROUBADOUR000/TimeFilter

provenance.licence: cc-by-4.0 (dataset card of the Hugging Face repository)
provenance.upstream: the processed ECL benchmark distributed by Autoformer/TimesNet (Time-Series-Library README: 'well-preprocessed datasets'); derived from UCI ElectricityLoadDiagrams20112014 (Trindade 2015), 321 clients, hourly; the processing steps are the distributors', not re-derived here
provenance.fetched_by: curl, pinned revision; digest verified against the LFS oid

dataset.column_order: the file's own order: date, 0..319, OT (features M: every channel is input and target)

partitions.rule: Dataset_Custom: num_train = int(0.7 n), num_test = int(0.2 n), num_vali = n - train - test; borders [0, train), [train - L, train + vali), [n - test - L, n); windows = rows - L - T + 1 per split

preprocessing.scaler: sklearn StandardScaler fit on the TRAIN rows [0, train) of every channel, applied to all rows (scale=True)
preprocessing.inverse: none: metrics in the normalized space (--inverse False)
preprocessing.time_marks: timeF features, freq h; consumed by the loader, unused by TimeFilter

training.loss: nn.MSELoss() + 0.05 x MoE routing loss (hard-coded alpha in train())
training.lr_schedule: adjust_learning_rate lradj=cosine: lr_e = lr/2 (1 + cos(e / train_epochs pi)) set after epoch e
training.batch: batch_size from the script; train loader shuffle=True, drop_last=False
training.epochs: train_epochs from the script; EarlyStopping(patience from run.py default, delta 0) on the validation MSE (no MoE term)
training.checkpoint: the lowest-validation-loss epoch's state_dict (checkpoint.pth), reloaded before test()
training.test_loss_printed_each_epoch: the author's train() evaluates the test loss every epoch for logging only; early stopping uses the validation loss

evaluation.scorer: utils.metrics.metric(preds, trues) on the concatenated float32 test predictions: MAE = mean|.|, MSE = mean(.)^2 over every window x step x channel
evaluation.test_loader: shuffle=False, drop_last=False, batch_size from the script
evaluation.aggregation: one mean per horizon; the paper averages the four horizons

seeds.author: run.py fixes random/torch/numpy seeds to 2021 and offers no CLI path to vary it; the paper reports three runs
seeds.how: the same three calls (random.seed, torch.manual_seed, np.random.seed) with each seed

operational_patches.what: import shims for sktime.datasets and patoolib
operational_patches.why: author modules import them at module level for UEA/M4 paths not on the forecasting path
operational_patches.effect: none: the shims refuse any call; verified by tests

operational_patches.why: run.py hard-codes fix_seed 2021; the paper reports three runs
the author's test() saves no arrays (np.save lines commented out)
operational_patches.effect: none: the author's return value is passed through; the captured arrays are the ones the author scores

operational_patches.what: np.Inf restored as an alias of np.inf before importing the author modules
operational_patches.why: NumPy 2 removed the alias; utils/tools.py EarlyStopping initialises val_loss_min = np.Inf
operational_patches.effect: none: the same float object the author's NumPy named; verified by tests

paper_code_disagreements: paper A.3 / Table 6 give lr 1e-3, e_layers 2, d_model 512, d_ff 512, patch 32, epochs 15 for Electricity and batch 16; the script adds dropout 0.5 (h96) / 0.4 (h192-720) and leaves patience (3), lradj (cosine), n_heads (4), alpha (0.1), top_p (0.5), pos (1), use_norm (1) at run.py defaults: not stated in the paper
Table 9 says L searched in {192, 336, 512, 720}; the script offers only L = 512 (patch 128, top_p 0.0) for the long-horizon runs
requirements.txt omits sktime and patool which the code imports
the paper reports the std over three runs; run.py has one fixed seed (2021)

agreement.rule: per horizon and for the four-horizon average, the three-seed mean of the replicated metric agrees with the published value when |mean - published| <= 2 x std_paper + 0.0005 (rounding half-unit); PARTIAL when <= 3 x std_paper + 0.0005; DISAGREEMENT otherwise. std_paper is the paper's std over its three runs of the four-horizon average (Table 7), applied per horizon as the only dispersion the paper reports; the replicated seed dispersion is reported beside it and never replaces the criterion

replay.reading: a GPU-trained float32 checkpoint reloaded in a fresh process through the author's test() on CPU: kernel-level differences are expected around 1e-6..1e-5 in normalized units; the metric recomputed from the replayed predictions must be within 1e-5 of the stored one; both maxima are always reported

metric_recompute.author_float32: bitwise equal to the record (same arrays, same function)

replay_rule.reading: a GPU-trained float32 checkpoint reloaded in a fresh process through the author's test() on CPU: kernel-level differences are expected around 1e-6..1e-5 in normalized units; the metric recomputed from the replayed predictions must be within 1e-5 of the stored one; both maxima are always reported
